title: Hydrogen Peroxide Standard Measurement Protocol
author: Peter Havel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ypqfvmw
materials: for a typical standard curve. Table

steps.title: Prepare Standard Wells
steps.instruction: Add the standard and water to the designated standard wells on the plate.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µl of standard (tubes A-G) per well.
Add 10 µl of HPLC-grade water per well.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Wells
steps.instruction: Prepare sample wells, ensuring each sample has at least two wells without catalase and two wells with catalase.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µl of sample to both the sample and sample + catalase wells.
Add 10 µl of catalase to the catalase wells.
Add 10 µl of HPLC-grade water to the non-catalase wells.

steps.title: Incubate Plate
steps.instruction: Add working reagent and incubate the plate.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µl of Working Reagent to each well.
Cover the plate with the plate cover.
Incubate on a shaker for one hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Remove the plate cover and read the absorbance at 595 nm using a plate reader.

steps.title: Calculate H2O2 Concentration
steps.instruction: Process the absorbance data to determine the H2O2 concentration of the samples.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the average absorbance of each standard, sample, and sample + catalase.
Subtract the average absorbance of standard A from itself and from all other standards and samples (including catalase containing samples).
Plot the corrected absorbance of standards as a function of the final H2O2 concentration (µM) from Table 1 to create a standard curve.
Subtract the catalase sample absorbance from the non-catalase sample absorbance to obtain the corrected sample absorbance.
Calculate the H2O2 concentration of the samples using the equation from the linear regression of the standard curve, substituting the corrected absorbance values.
